## 4.0.0-draft.3 — 2026-10-17

- Added immutable, validated import of diK Wikidata-only catalogs; preserves existing curated/external layers, re-registers as a separate canonical v9 Logical Artifact and requires explicit catalog selection.
- Replaced simple rollback-on-exception canonical graph registration with a journalled recoverable two-file registration. Added status/finish/rollback CLI and simulated crash regression tests.
- Clarified Authoring Kit (canonical producer) vs diK (dictionaries and proposals) vs Framework (contracts) responsibilities.
- Reconciled Framework draft.3 qualification claims with the actual prior reference-test scope.
- Remains draft: no arbitrary legacy migration, production power-loss qualification or real 300-language industrial benchmark.

## 4.0.0-draft.2 — 2026-10-16

- Qualified the v11 semantic demo against **actual** Framework draft.3 validators and diK coverage reference.
- Added shared Framework SHA-256 pin identical to Integration Pack v11, plus `qualify-v11` CLI / offline verifier.
- Added read-only three-way coverage match between Authoring Kit, Framework and Integration Pack; rejects changed pinned schemas.
- Preserved the historical v9 build files received separately in `authkit.zip`; no canonical history rewritten.
- Added independent cross-repo qualification tests and validation guidance; no hosted publication or arbitrary legacy migration claim.

# 4.0.0-draft.1 — 2026-10-16

- Added opt-in Framework v11 namespaced KQ/KP/KA/KS authoring profile; historical v9/v10 semantics and workspace formats unchanged.
- Added explicit registration/validation gate for graph, registry, external Wikidata crosswalk, and language catalog.
- Added diK-compatible coverage-v11 direct/fallback/missing reports for KQ and KP by locale.
- Added reviewed plan checks and limited all-approved, digest-bound conversion into a **new complete v11-shaped graph** with v9 Logical Artifact registration; original bytes remain untouched.
- Introduced safe identity-role manifest, negative regression tests, and v11 integration documentation.
- Draft caveat: independent byte-level validation against Framework v11 draft.3 schemas remains pending exact source archive availability.

# Changelog

## 3.3.1 — Consumer preflight and local snapshot consolidation

- New read-only `audit-discovery` CLI: absent/incomplete/invalid/stale/fresh and safe generic fallback.
- Reader hints are explicitly **not** Manager inventory, access grants or C2/C4 publication approvals.
- Consumer-facing contract guidance and regression tests for Manager/Konstellation/Light integration.
- Drop outdated generated `SMARTDUMP_INDEX.txt` and `SNAPSHOT_INDEX.txt` from this updated package.
- Add root `Nettoyer_Anciens_Fichiers.pyw` UI for explicit, hash-guarded deletion of the original local copies only.
- No v9 canon, local-workspace envelope, or v1 Discovery schema changes.


## 3.3.0 — Noncanonical discovery and reader specialization

- Add deterministic root `kristal.discovery/1.0` metadata, reader inventory and advisory reader profile, generated by `init`, `classify`, `build-discovery`, and `build-v9`.
- Add an optional workspace Arketype `classification` contract and CLI catalog resolution (`PRF-xx` to `ARK-xx`), preserving unknown legacy types and reading the older sidecar only as an unverified hint.
- Expose observed local size, manifest segment declarations, missing/remote flags, reader candidates, fingerprint and non-authority constraints. No whole-project size, JSON depth, record size, or semantic cardinality is invented.
- Add derived reader files to the read surface and expose discovery in read-only `inspect`.
- Preserve v9 Logical/State Commitment, workspace v3.2 envelope, independent qualification and publication gates.


## 3.2.5-rc.1 — V10 integration hardening candidate (English)

- No workspace, State Index, Logical Artifact or v9 State Commitment contract changes.
- Restrict GitHub read-surface index paths to safe workspace reader roots and verify indexed **size and SHA-256** before reporting readiness; reject duplicate/disallowed paths.
- Add read-only `audit_workspace_migration.py` for comparing canon/state identity and available v9 commitments between independently staged workspaces.
- Add eight regression tests for read-surface determinism, tampering, disabled-AI staleness, remote materialization availability and migration audits.
- Update v10/Manager/C1/C2/C3 guidance in English, including the requirement for authorization before **public sync**.
- Preserve the 3.2.4 tool baseline and example commitments; new candidate version must be independently accepted by consumers.


## 3.2.4 — GitHub AI read-surface alignment

- aucun changement de `kristal.local-workspace/3.2.0`, des Logical Commitments ou du State Commitment ;
- nouveau contrat dérivé `kristal.github-read-surface/1.0` et commande read-only `read-surface` ;
- `inspect` expose la read surface exacte et `kristals/<slug>` comme racine de collection suggérée ;
- `build-ai` indexe maintenant les Materialization Manifests v9 et décrit séparément leurs blobs/locators comme objets de transport ;
- `ai/COVERAGE.json` expose disponibilité locale, locators externes et locators locaux manquants ;
- `AI_MANIFEST.json` documente la matérialisation et le contrat de projection GitHub ;
- `pack-ai` et le sync GitHub peuvent partager la même liste de lecture afin d'éviter le drift entre capsule et repo ;
- la read surface exclut tooling/build/release/hosting/runtime et reste distincte de la publication v10 ;
- support explicite du modèle `URL GitHub → AI_START_HERE.md → ai/INDEX.json → fichiers ciblés`, adapté aux grandes collections.

## 3.2.1 — Local-toolchain alignment

- aucun changement du format `kristal.local-workspace/3.2.0` ni des profils de commitment ;
- terminologie utilisateur harmonisée vers **Local Kristal / Local Kit** ;
- chemins d'interop v9 documentés pour Manager/Kompiler/Setup : `state/`, `build/v9/`, `release/v9/states/**/` ;
- responsabilités explicites : Manager = inventaire/backup, GitHub Setup = qualify/publish/activate, Kompiler = lecture/context optionnelle ;
- nettoyage des références UX v3.1/Authoring sans réécrire les identifiants legacy nécessaires à la migration.

## 3.2.0 — Local Kristals / toolchain separation

- UX et format racine alignés sur la notion de **Local Kristal** : `kristal.local-workspace/3.2.0` ;
- `build-v9` construit seulement le state v9 par défaut ;
- la couche `kristal.portable-ai/1.0` devient explicitement **optionnelle** ;
- `build-v9 --with-ai`, `build-ai`, `check-ai` et `pack-ai` restent disponibles ;
- `init --with-ai` permet de préparer immédiatement la couche IA, sinon elle n'est pas créée ;
- `check` n'exige plus `AI_START_HERE.md` pour un Local Kristal normal ;
- `pack` n'effectue plus de build IA implicite ;
- **Kristal Manager** est désigné comme propriétaire de l'inventaire et du backup GitHub public/privé des dossiers locaux ;
- **Kristal GitHub Setup/Bootstrap** est désigné comme workflow principal pour qualification, publication et activation réseau ;
- `github-qualify` / `github-publish` restent comme commandes de compatibilité avancée et affichent un avertissement ;
- **Kompiler** est explicitement un consommateur optionnel/read tool, pas un gestionnaire de lifecycle ;
- suppression des wrappers PowerShell `Qualify-Kristal.ps1`, `Publish-Kristal.ps1`, `Export-Kristal.ps1` ;
- migration v1/v2/v3/v3.1 → v3.2 sans modification du State Index v9 ;
- les workspaces v3.1 possédant déjà une couche IA la conservent et la marquent `portable_ai.enabled=true`.

## 3.1.0 — Portable AI / offline-first reading

- workspace `kristal.authoring-workspace/3.1.0` ;
- nouveau profil dérivé `kristal.portable-ai/1.0` ;
- `AI_START_HERE.md` à la racine comme point d'entrée universel pour une IA qui reçoit le dossier/ZIP ;
- génération automatique par `build-v9` de `AI_MANIFEST.json`, `ai/CONTEXT.md`, `ai/INDEX.json`, `ai/GLOSSARY.md`, `ai/RELATIONS.json`, `ai/COVERAGE.json`, `ai/QUESTIONS.md` et `state/state-snapshot.json` ;
- la copie portable du State Snapshot est byte-for-byte identique au build v9 ;
- aucun besoin de GitHub, réseau, Python, Node ou tooling Kristal pour **lire** la capsule ;
- nouvelles commandes `build-ai`, `check-ai`, `pack-ai` ;
- `pack-ai` produit un ZIP déterministe épuré qui exclut tooling, hosting, build, release, validation et tests ;
- les fichiers du read model sont indexés avec rôle, media type, taille et SHA-256 ;
- couverture explicite de l'ownership, des limites et des références sémantiques externes pinées ;
- aucune référence externe n'est téléchargée silencieusement ;
- glossaire authored via `docs/08_GLOSSARY.md`, projeté dans `ai/GLOSSARY.md` sans invention ;
- migration v3.0 → v3.1 sans modification du State Index v9 ;
- GitHub reste une option de transport/qualification/publication v10 et ne devient pas une dépendance de lecture.
